nodes.summary: Given a clause $C$ and a state whose next free vertex is $n$, the literals of $C$ are read from the last one. If $C$ is empty, the new state has next free vertex $n + 1$, the same earlier occurrences, and the emitted edges followed by $(n, 0)$, $(n, 1)$, $(n, 2)$, joining the fresh vertex $n$ to the palette vertices $0$, $1$, $2$. Otherwise let $l$ be the last literal of $C$ and $ls$ the other literals in reverse…
nodes.title: Processing one clause in the 3-COLOR construction

nodes.summary: Given a list of literals, a vertex $o$ (the output so far) and a state, the result is defined by recursion on the list. For the empty list, the emitted edges of the state are followed by $(o, 1)$ and $(o, 2)$, joining $o$ to the palette vertices $1$ and $2$, and the other components are unchanged. For a list with head $l$ and tail $ls$, first add an occurrence of $l$, obtaining a state and the literal vertex $L$;…
nodes.title: Processing the remaining literals of a clause

nodes.summary: Given a literal $l = (x, b)$ with variable index $x$ and polarity $b$, and a state whose next free vertex is $n$, let $L = n$ and $M = n + 1$. The new state has next free vertex $n + 2$, records the occurrence $(x, b, L, M)$ at the front of the list of earlier occurrences, and appends to the emitted edges first $(L, M)$, $(L, 2)$, $(M, 2)$ (a triangle with the palette vertex $2$), then the consistency edges of the…
nodes.title: Adding a literal occurrence in the 3-COLOR construction

nodes.summary: Given vertices $a$ and $o$ and a state whose next free vertex is $n$, let $u = n$, $v = n + 1$ and $w = n + 2$. The new state has next free vertex $n + 3$, the same earlier occurrences, and the emitted edges followed by $(a, u)$, $(o, v)$, $(u, v)$, $(u, w)$, $(v, w)$, $(w, 2)$. The result is this new state together with the output vertex $w$.
nodes.title: OR gadget of the 3-COLOR construction

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, start from the state whose next free vertex is $3$, with no earlier occurrences and with emitted edges $(0, 1)$, $(0, 2)$, $(1, 2)$ (the palette triangle on the vertices $0$, $1$, $2$), and process the clauses of $\varphi$ one at a time, from the last clause to the first. The result is the final state.
nodes.title: The SAT-to-3-COLOR graph construction

nodes.summary: A state of the graph construction reducing CNF satisfiability to 3-colorability consists of a natural number, the next free vertex; a list of quadruples $(x, b, L, M)$ of a variable index $x$, a polarity $b$, the vertex $L$ of the literal and the vertex $M$ of its negation, recording the earlier literal occurrences with the latest first; and a list of pairs of natural numbers, the edges emitted so far, in emission…
nodes.title: State of the SAT-to-3-COLOR construction

nodes.summary: The decision problem 3-COLOR accepts a bit string $x$ exactly when there are a natural number $n$ and a list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers such that $x$ is the encoding of $n$ and $es$ ($n$ in unary, then each edge $(u, v)$ as $u$ and $v$ in unary), every edge $(u, v)$ in $es$ has $u < n$ and $v < n$, and the graph on $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with edge list $es$ (symmetrized, loops dropped) is $3$-colorable.
nodes.title: 3-COLOR

nodes.summary: Let $l = (x, b)$ be a literal with variable index $x$ and polarity $b$, let $L$, $M$ be the vertices of a new occurrence of $l$, and let $(x', b', L', M')$ be an earlier occurrence. If $x' \ne x$ the list of consistency edges is empty. If $x' = x$ and $b' = b$ it is $[(L', M), (M', L)]$; if $x' = x$ and $b' \ne b$ it is $[(L', L), (M', M)]$.
nodes.title: Consistency edges between two occurrences of a variable

nodes.summary: To decode a bit string $x$, read a unary number $n$ from the front of $x$ ($n$ copies of true ended by false); if there is none, decoding fails. Otherwise decode the rest of $x$ as an edge list $es$ (pairs of unary numbers until the input ends); if that fails, decoding fails, and otherwise the result is the pair $(n, es)$.
nodes.title: Decoding a graph

nodes.summary: The edge-list decoder, applied to the empty bit string, succeeds and returns the empty edge list.
nodes.title: Decoding the empty input

nodes.summary: If $x$ is a nonempty bit string and reading a unary length prefix from $x$ fails, then the edge-list decoder fails on $x$.
nodes.title: The edge-list decoder fails on a cut-off first number

nodes.summary: If reading a unary length prefix from a bit string $x$ returns a number $u$ and the remaining suffix $r$, and reading a unary length prefix from $r$ fails, then the edge-list decoder fails on $x$.
nodes.title: Decoding fails on a dangling half-pair

nodes.summary: The edge-list decoder reads a bit string as a list of pairs of natural numbers, each number written in unary as that many $1$s followed by a $0$. On the empty string it returns the empty list. Otherwise it reads a number $u$, then a number $v$, decodes the rest recursively, and returns $(u, v)$ followed by the result; it fails if the input ends inside a number or after an unpaired number, or if decoding the rest…
nodes.title: Edge-list decoder

nodes.summary: The edge bits of a list of pairs of natural numbers are the concatenation, over its pairs $(u, v)$ in order, of $u$ ones, a zero, $v$ ones and a zero.
nodes.title: Bit encoding of an edge list

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers, the graph of $es$ on $n$ vertices is the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $(i, j)$ or $(j, i)$ belongs to $es$. Loops are dropped, and pairs with an endpoint at least $n$ contribute no edge.
nodes.title: Graph of an edge list

nodes.summary: The graph encoding of a number $n$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers is the bit string that writes $n$ in unary and then, for each pair $(u, v)$ of $E$ in order, writes $u$ and then $v$ in unary, where a natural number $k$ is written in unary as $k$ ones followed by one zero.
nodes.title: Bit-string encoding of a graph

nodes.summary: If reading a unary length prefix from a bit string $x$ succeeds with value $u$ and unconsumed suffix $r$, then $r$ is strictly shorter than $x$.
nodes.title: Reading a unary number shortens the input

nodes.summary: This is the graph encoding of the number $4$ and the edge list $(0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 3), (1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3)$, in that order, that is, of the complete graph on the vertices $0, 1, 2, 3$.
nodes.title: The complete graph on four vertices as a bit string

nodes.summary: The map sends a bit string $x$ that decodes to a CNF formula $\varphi$ to the 3-COLOR instance of $\varphi$, and sends every bit string that does not decode to a CNF formula to the graph encoding of the number $4$ and the edge list $(0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 3), (1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3)$, in that order, that is, of the complete graph on four vertices.
nodes.title: The SAT to 3-COLOR reduction map on bit strings

nodes.summary: Run the gadget construction on a CNF formula $\varphi$; it ends with a next free vertex $N$ and a list of emitted edges. The 3-COLOR instance of $\varphi$ is the graph encoding of the number $N$ and the emitted edges in reverse order.
nodes.title: The 3-COLOR instance of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: A CNF formula $\varphi$ is satisfiable if and only if the graph built from $\varphi$ by the Garey–Johnson–Stockmeyer construction is 3-colorable. Here, writing $n$ for the number of vertices the construction allocates, the graph has vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, and two distinct vertices are adjacent when the construction emits an edge between them in either order.
nodes.title: Correctness of the reduction from SAT to 3-coloring

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a construction state, let $v : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be an assignment, and let $c : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1, 2\}$ be a coloring. Then $c$ colors $s$ according to $v$ when $c(0) = 0$, $c(1) = 1$ and $c(2) = 2$ (the palette vertices $T$, $F$, $B$), $c(a) \ne c(b)$ for every edge $(a, b)$ emitted in $s$, and for every occurrence recorded in $s$ with variable $x$, polarity $b$, literal vertex $L$ and…
nodes.title: Colorings that follow an assignment

nodes.summary: A construction state $s$ with next free vertex $n$ is well formed when $3 \le n$; every emitted edge $(a, b)$ has $a < n$, $b < n$ and $a \ne b$; the literal vertex and the negation vertex of every recorded occurrence are smaller than $n$; the pairs $(0, 1)$, $(0, 2)$ and $(1, 2)$ are emitted edges (the palette triangle); for every recorded occurrence with literal vertex $L$ and negation vertex $M$, the pairs…
nodes.title: Well-formed construction states

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a construction state with next free vertex $m$, let $n \ge m$, and let $E$ be a list of pairs of natural numbers. Then the state with next free vertex $n$, the same recorded occurrences as $s$, and emitted edges those of $s$ followed by $E$ extends $s$: its next free vertex is at least that of $s$, and its emitted edges and recorded occurrences include those of $s$.
nodes.title: Extending a state makes it grow

nodes.summary: A construction state $s'$ extends a construction state $s$ when the next free vertex of $s'$ is at least that of $s$, every edge emitted in $s$ is emitted in $s'$, and every occurrence recorded in $s$ is recorded in $s'$.
nodes.title: Growth of construction states

nodes.summary: For a literal $l$ and a state $s$ of the SAT-to-3-COLOR construction whose next free vertex is $n$, the state obtained by adding the occurrence $l$ to $s$ has next free vertex $n + 2$.
nodes.title: Adding a literal occurrence takes two new vertices

nodes.summary: A map $c : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1, 2\}$ properly colors a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers when $c(a) \ne c(b)$ for every pair $(a, b)$ in $E$.
nodes.title: Proper 3-colorings of an edge list

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$, both endpoints of every edge emitted by the construction for $\varphi$ are smaller than the number of vertices the construction allocates (its next free vertex).
nodes.title: The construction's edges lie below its vertex count

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $E$ a list of pairs $(a, b)$ of natural numbers with $a < n$, $b < n$ and $a \ne b$. The graph on $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with edge list $E$ is 3-colorable if and only if some map $c : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1, 2\}$ satisfies $c(a) \ne c(b)$ for every pair $(a, b)$ in $E$.
nodes.title: 3-colorability through colorings of the natural numbers

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers, decoding the graph encoding of $n$ and $es$ succeeds and returns $(n, es)$.
nodes.title: Graph decoding inverts graph encoding

nodes.summary: For every list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers, the edge-list decoder applied to the edge bits of $es$ succeeds and returns $es$.
nodes.title: Decoding the bits of an edge list

nodes.summary: If reading a unary length prefix from a bit string $x$ returns $u$ with remaining suffix $r$, and reading one from $r$ returns $v$ with remaining suffix $r'$, then the edge-list decoder succeeds on $x$ exactly when it succeeds on $r'$, and in that case its result on $x$ is its result on $r'$ with the pair $(u, v)$ put in front.
nodes.title: Decoding one pair, then the rest

nodes.summary: For every bit string $x$ and every list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers, if the edge-list decoder returns $es$ on $x$, then $x$ is the edge bits of $es$.
nodes.title: The edge-list decoder succeeds only on edge bits

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers, the graph encoding of $n$ and $es$ is $n$ ones, then a zero, then the edge bits of $es$.
nodes.title: Graph encoding as vertex count plus edge bits

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a bit string. If decoding $x$ as a graph yields a number $n$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, then $x$ is the graph encoding of $n$ and $E$.
nodes.title: Graph decoding succeeds only on encodings

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a well-formed construction state with next free vertex $m$, let $n \ge m$, and let $E$ be a list of pairs $(a, b)$ of natural numbers with $a < n$, $b < n$ and $a \ne b$. Then the state with next free vertex $n$, the same recorded occurrences as $s$, and emitted edges those of $s$ followed by $E$ is well formed.
nodes.title: Extending a well-formed state keeps it well formed

nodes.summary: The emitter has thirteen stacks: $T$ (tokens), $O$ (output), $N$ (the next free vertex), $R$ (the current OR output), $D$ (earlier occurrences), $E$ (the walk's other side), $A$ (the current name), $P$ (its polarity), $F$ (the first-literal flag), $U$ (an earlier literal vertex), and the scratch stacks $X$ and $B$ for comparisons and $W$ for copies.

nodes.summary: The code of a color $c \in \{0, 1, 2\}$ is the pair of bits whose first bit is $1$ iff $c = 2$ and whose second bit is $1$ iff $c = 1$: $0 \mapsto 00$, $1 \mapsto 01$ and $2 \mapsto 10$.

nodes.title: Acceptance condition of the 3-COLOR verifier

nodes.summary: The verifier accepts an input $x$ and a witness $w$ (bit strings) iff $x$ decodes to a number $n$ and an edge list $E$, every endpoint of an edge in $E$ is less than $n$, $w$ has at least $2n$ bits, every vertex $i < n$ has a valid color code in $w$ (bits $2i$ and $2i + 1$, not $11$), and the two ends of every edge $(u, v) \in E$ with $u \ne v$ have different color codes.
nodes.title: The 3-COLOR verifier

nodes.summary: For every $n$, every map $f$ from $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ to pairs of bits and every $i < n$, the color code of vertex $i$ in the flattening of the list $f(0), \dots, f(n - 1)$ is $f(i)$.
nodes.title: Color codes of a flattened coloring

nodes.summary: For every list $cs$ of pairs of bits and every natural number $i$, the color code of vertex $i$ in the flattening of $cs$ is the $i$-th pair of $cs$ (counting from $0$) if $i$ is less than the length of $cs$, and $00$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Color codes of flattened pairs

nodes.summary: The color code of vertex $i$ in a bit string $w$ is the pair of bits at positions $2i$ and $2i + 1$ of $w$ (counting from $0$), where a position past the end of $w$ reads as $0$. The codes $00$, $01$, $10$ stand for the colors $0$, $1$, $2$; $11$ is invalid.

nodes.summary: A bit string $x$ is in 3-COLOR iff some bit string $w$ of length at most $2|x|$ is accepted together with $x$ by the 3-COLOR verifier.
